[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Write the chemical formula of alum dust.","marks":1,"answer":"K₂SO₄.Al₂(SO₄)₃.24H₂O"},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Camphor is sublimated substance–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The substance which, while heating, turns directly from solid into gaseous state is known as sublimate. When heat is applied to solid camphor (C₁₀H₁₆O) then it turns into gaseous state without being liquid. So, it is a sublimate."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Equation (i) is redox reaction. Explain with equations.","marks":3,"answer":"(i) 4Na + O₂ → 2Na₂O
Oxidation half Reaction: 4Na - 4e⁻ → 4Na⁺
Reduction half Reaction: O₂ + 4e⁻ → 2O²⁻
Here, four sodium atoms donate four electrons and four Na⁺ ions are formed which means oxidation half reaction. These four electrons are accepted by O₂, which indicates reduction half reaction. In this reaction, acid and base neutralize each other producing salt and water. So, it is acid-base neutralization reaction. In this reaction electron exchange does not occur. So, it is non-redox reaction.
Reaction (iii): FeSO₄ + 2NaOH → Fe(OH)₂↓ + Na₂SO₄
Here, Fe(OH)₂ gets precipitate for its low solubility. So, it is precipitation reaction. In this reaction, electron exchange does not occur. So, it is also a non-redox reaction.
So, (ii) and (iii) both are non-redox reaction but they don't show same type of reaction.
---"}]

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"Molecular weight of nitrogen means that the mass of 1 mole nitrogen molecule or 6.023 × 10²³ nitrogen molecules is 28g."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the oxidation number of sulfur in X of stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction: 2Na + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + H₂
X is Na₂SO₄.
Let, oxidation number of S be \(x\).
∴ \(+1 \times 2 + x + (-2) \times 4 = 0\)
or, \(2 + x - 8 = 0\)
∴ \(x = +6\)
Oxidation number of S in Na₂SO₄ is +6."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In the reaction of above stem analyse that–“reduction is not possible without oxidation.”","marks":4,"answer":"Reduction reaction means acceptance of electrons. In this reaction H⁺ of H₂SO₄ accepted electron and converted to H. So this is the reduction half reaction: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. The reaction in which any species loses its electrons is known as oxidation half reaction: 2Na – 2e⁻ → 2Na⁺. In this reaction Na loses electrons which are accepted by H⁺. So, in this reaction oxidation and reduction take place simultaneously. Thus, reduction is not possible without oxidation.
---"}]

‘A’ is MgSO₄.
In MgSO₄, oxidation number of O = -2, oxidation number of Mg = +2.
Let oxidation number of S = \(x\).
From the chemical formula: \(+2 \times 1 + x + (-2) \times 4 = 0\)
\(x = +6\)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"From the two reactions of the stem. one is redox reaction but another one is not redox–Analyze.","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (i): 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO

Reaction (ii): MgO + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂O
This is an acid-base neutralization reaction. In this case, no electron is transferred. So, it is not an oxidation-reduction reaction.

question:
(i) N₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO(g); ΔH = +180 kJ
(ii) 2K + Cl₂ → 2KCl
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Isomer?","marks":1,"answer":"Two compounds with similar molecular formula but with different structural formula are called isomers of each other."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain the metallic bond.","marks":2,"answer":"In the metal lattice, the atom of the metal donates electron from their outermost energy level and turns into a positive ion. These delocalized electrons create a sea of electrons. Those positive ions remain organized in this sea of electron. When a delocalized electron is situated in the midst of two metallic ions, both the ions are attracted towards the electron with an electrostatic force. This causes the two ions to remain connected, these kinds of bonds are called metallic bond."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain the electron transfer process of the reaction (ii) of stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction: 2K + Cl₂ → 2KCl
Oxidation half-reaction : 2K - 2e⁻ → 2K⁺ (K is reductant)
Reduction half-reaction: Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻ (Cl is oxidant)
This reaction can be expressed as below:
2K + Cl₂ → 2K⁺ + 2Cl⁻ (Then they combine to form 2KCl)
Therefore, electron transfers occur in reaction no. (ii)"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the effect of heat, pressure and concentration in equilibrium of reaction (i).","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction: N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g); ΔH = +180 kJ (Endothermic)
Effect of heat: Since ΔH is positive, it is an endothermic reaction. Applying heat (increasing temperature) shifts equilibrium to the right, increasing NO production. Removing heat shifts it left.
Effect of Pressure: The difference in moles of gas between reactants (1+1=2) and products (2) is zero. Therefore, pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.
Effect of Concentration: Increasing concentration of N₂ or O₂ shifts equilibrium to the right, increasing NO. Increasing concentration of NO or decreasing N₂/O₂ shifts equilibrium to the left.
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
(i) 2K + Cl₂ → 2A
(ii) Mg(OH)₂ + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + 2H₂O
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is molecule?","marks":1,"answer":"A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that retains its chemical properties and is capable of independent existence. It consists of two or more atoms chemically bonded together."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"All addition reaction are not synthesis reaction–Explain with example.","marks":2,"answer":"Addition reactions combine two or more compounds or elements to form new compounds. Synthesis reactions are addition reactions where only elements combine to form a compound.
Example of addition but not synthesis: 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃ (Reactants include compounds).
Example of addition and synthesis: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl (Reactants are only elements).
So, all synthesis reactions are addition reactions, but not all addition reactions are synthesis reactions."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Compound 'A' in stem (i) is soluble in water. Explain with reason.","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction: 2K + Cl₂ → 2KCl. So, compound A is KCl. It is an ionic compound. When dissolved in water, the positive K⁺ ions are attracted to the negative oxygen pole of water molecules, and the negative Cl⁻ ions are attracted to the positive hydrogen pole of water molecules. This interaction overcomes the ionic lattice energy, making KCl soluble in water."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Comparing the above two reactions on the basis of electron exchange.","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (i): 2K + Cl₂ → 2KCl. This is a redox reaction.
Oxidation: 2K - 2e⁻ → 2K⁺
Reduction: Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻
Electron exchange occurs.
Reaction (ii): Mg(OH)₂ + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + 2H₂O. This is an acid-base neutralization (double displacement) reaction. There is no change in the oxidation states of any atom (Mg remains +2, O remains -2, H remains +1, S remains +6). Therefore, no electron exchange occurs.
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
(i) 36.8% of nitrogen and 63.2% of oxygen are found after analyzing the compound A. The molecular mass of the compound is 76.
ii. SO₂ + O₂ → SO₃
iii. H₂ + S → H₂S
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is mole?","marks":1,"answer":"The amount of a chemical substance containing Avogadro's number (6.02 × 10²³) of molecules, atoms or ions is called mole of that substance."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain that the valency of nitrogen and valence electron are different.","marks":2,"answer":"Electron configuration of nitrogen: N(7) = 1s² 2s² 2p³. The element has 5 electrons in its valence shell (2nd level), so its valence electron number is 5. It has 3 unpaired electrons and can form 3 covalent bonds to achieve stability. Therefore, its valency is 3. Hence, valency (3) and valence electron number (5) are different."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Determine the molecular formula of the compound 'A' of the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"Step 1: Find the empirical formula.
Element: N | O
Percentage: 36.8 | 63.2
Atomic mass: 14 | 16
Mole ratio: 36.8/14 = 2.63 | 63.2/16 = 3.95
Simple ratio: 2.63/2.63 ≈ 1 | 3.95/2.63 ≈ 1.5
To get whole numbers, multiply by 2: 2 | 3
Empirical formula = N₂O₃
Step 2: Find molecular formula.
Empirical formula mass = (14×2) + (16×3) = 28 + 48 = 76
Given molecular mass = 76
n = Molecular mass / Empirical formula mass = 76/76 = 1
Molecular formula = (N₂O₃)₁ = N₂O₃"},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the oxidation number of sulphur in sulphur compounds of reaction number (ii) and number (iii).","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (ii): 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃
In SO₂: Let oxidation state of S be \(x\). \(x + 2(-2) = 0\) => \(x = +4\)
In SO₃: \(x + 3(-2) = 0\) => \(x = +6\)
Sulphur's oxidation number increases from +4 to +6 (Oxidation).
Reaction (iii): H₂ + S → H₂S
In S (elemental): Oxidation state = 0.
In H₂S: \(2(+1) + x = 0\) => \(x = -2\)
Sulphur's oxidation number decreases from 0 to -2 (Reduction).
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
Complete the reaction below:
(i) PbCl₂ + Cl₂ → PbCl₄
(ii) 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is latent valency?","marks":1,"answer":"Latent valency is defined as the difference between the highest valency and active valency of an element."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Show the differences between Cl₂ and 2Cl.","marks":2,"answer":"Cl₂: Represents a molecule of chlorine gas. Two chlorine atoms are bonded by a covalent bond.
2Cl: Represents two separate, unbonded chlorine atoms."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Oxidation reduction reaction is simultaneous. Explain with the help of reaction (i).","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction (i): PbCl₂ + Cl₂ → PbCl₄
In PbCl₂, Pb has oxidation state +2. In PbCl₄, Pb has oxidation state +4.
Oxidation: Pb²⁺ → Pb⁴⁺ + 2e⁻
The Cl₂ molecule (oxidation state 0) gains these 2 electrons: Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻ (forming part of PbCl₄).
The electron loss (oxidation) and electron gain (reduction) happen in the same step. Therefore, oxidation and reduction are simultaneous."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"All the synthesis reaction is addition reaction but all the addition reaction is not synthesis reaction.—Evaluate with reactions (i) and (ii) in the stem.","marks":4,"answer":"Synthesis Reaction: Two or more elements combine to form one product.
Addition Reaction: Two or more substances combine to form one product (reactants can be elements or compounds).
Reaction (ii): 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl. Reactants are elements (Na, Cl₂). It is both a synthesis and an addition reaction.
Reaction (i): PbCl₂ + Cl₂ → PbCl₄. Reactants are a compound (PbCl₂) and an element (Cl₂). It is an addition reaction but not a synthesis reaction (because not all reactants are elements).
This demonstrates that all synthesis reactions are addition reactions, but not all addition reactions are synthesis reactions.
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
(i) A(g) + 3B(g) → 2D(g); ΔH = x kJ/mol
(ii) Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is reversible reaction?","marks":1,"answer":"The reaction in which the reactants react and convert to products and at the same time the products react again and convert to reactants is called reversible reaction."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Chemical equilibria is dynamic–Explain it.","marks":2,"answer":"At equilibrium, the forward and backward reactions occur at equal rates. The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant, but the reactions do not stop. Molecules are continuously being converted in both directions. Hence, it is a dynamic state, not a static one."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"From reaction (ii) show that the oxidation reduction reaction occurs simultaneously.","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Ionic form: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.
Oxidation: Zn loses 2 electrons: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻
Reduction: Cu²⁺ gains 2 electrons: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu
The electrons lost by Zn are immediately gained by Cu²⁺ in the same reaction mixture. Therefore, oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Discuss the effects of temperature and pressure on the equilibria of reaction (i).","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (i): A(g) + 3B(g) ⇌ 2D(g); ΔH = x kJ/mol
Effect of Temperature:
If x is negative (exothermic), increasing temperature shifts equilibrium left; decreasing temperature shifts it right.
If x is positive (endothermic), increasing temperature shifts equilibrium right; decreasing temperature shifts it left.
Effect of Pressure: There are 4 moles of gas on left (1+3) and 2 moles on right.
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer moles (to the right).
Decreasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with more moles (to the left).
---"}]

subject: Chemistry
question:
(i) 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃
(ii) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g); ΔH = -198 kJ
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is the rate of reaction?","marks":1,"answer":"The amount of products produced from reactants per unit time is called the rate of reaction."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Explain how the reversible reaction can be made into irreversible reaction?","marks":2,"answer":"An irreversible reaction is one where products cannot revert to reactants. A reversible reaction can be made irreversible if one of the products is continuously removed from the reaction medium. For example: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). If the CO₂ gas is allowed to escape, CaO cannot react with it to form CaCO₃ back, making it irreversible."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Explain that the reaction (i) is a redox reaction.","marks":3,"answer":"Reaction: 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃
Oxidation: Fe²⁺ loses 1 electron: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻
Reduction: Cl₂ gains 2 electrons: Cl₂ + 2e⁻ → 2Cl⁻ (Two Fe²⁺ ions provide the 2e⁻)
Since there is both loss (oxidation) and gain (reduction) of electrons, it is a redox reaction."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the effect of heat on the reversible reaction in (ii) according to the Le-Chatelier principle.","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (ii): 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g); ΔH = -198 kJ (Exothermic)
According to Le Chatelier's principle, if a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to counteract the change.
Effect of adding heat (increasing temperature): The reaction is exothermic (releases heat). Adding heat is like adding a product. To counteract this, the equilibrium shifts in the endothermic direction (the reverse reaction, which absorbs heat). Therefore, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the left, decreasing SO₃ yield.
Effect of removing heat (decreasing temperature): This favors the exothermic forward reaction to produce heat. Equilibrium shifts to the right, increasing SO₃ yield.
---"}]

parts:

This stability is called chemical equilibrium."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Cl⁻ is a reductant—Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"A reductant is a substance that donates electrons and gets oxidized. Cl⁻ ion can donate an electron to become Cl atom (which dimerizes to Cl₂). For example: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Therefore, Cl⁻ acts as a reductant."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Calculate the number of atoms in 10 grams of the compound produced in the stem.","marks":3,"answer":"The compound produced is SO₃.
Molar mass of SO₃ = 32 + (16×3) = 80 g/mol.
Number of moles in 10g = 10/80 = 0.125 mol.
Number of molecules = 0.125 × 6.023 × 10²³ = 7.53 × 10²² molecules.
Each SO₃ molecule contains 4 atoms (1 S + 3 O).
Total number of atoms = 7.53 × 10²² × 4 = 3.01 × 10²³ atoms."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the effect of temperature and pressure on the reaction mentioned in the stem in chemical equilibrium.","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g); ΔH = -196 kJ (Exothermic)
Effect of Temperature: The forward reaction is exothermic.
Increasing temperature favors the endothermic reverse reaction. Equilibrium shifts left, decreasing SO₃.
Decreasing temperature favors the exothermic forward reaction. Equilibrium shifts right, increasing SO₃.
Effect of Pressure: There are 3 moles of gas on left (2+1) and 2 moles on right.
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with fewer moles (right), increasing SO₃.
Decreasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the side with more moles (left), decreasing SO₃.
---"}]

Moles of gas: Left side = 2, Right side = 4+1 = 5.

parts:

Melting point (0°C for water) is the temperature at which solid (ice) gains enough energy to overcome lattice forces and become liquid.
Boiling point (100°C for water) is the temperature at which liquid gains enough energy to overcome intermolecular forces and become vapor. Molar mass KOH = 56 g/mol. Moles of KOH = 25/56 ≈ 0.446 mol.
Stoichiometry requires 2 mol KOH per 1 mol H₂SO₄. For 0.51 mol H₂SO₄, required KOH = 1.02 mol. We have only 0.446 mol. Therefore, KOH is the limiting reactant.
From the equation, 2 mol KOH (112g) produce 1 mol K₂SO₄ (174g).
Amount of K₂SO₄ from 25g KOH = (174 / 112) × 25 = 38.84 g."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In which reaction oxidation reduction has occurred between two reactions of stem? Analyze with logic.","marks":4,"answer":"Reaction (ii) is a redox reaction.

Reduction: 2H⁺ (+1) + 2e⁻ → H₂ (0)
Electron transfer occurs.
Reaction (i): H₂SO₄ + 2KOH → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O
No change in oxidation states. H remains +1, O remains -2, S remains +6, K remains +1.
It is a neutralization (double displacement) reaction, not redox.
